63		p.Lifecycle.Append(
64			cell.Hook{
65				OnStart: func(ctx cell.HookContext) error {
66					if err := autoCreatePools(
67						ctx,
68						p.Clientset.CiliumV2alpha1().CiliumResourceIPPools(),
69						p.Cfg.AutoCreateCiliumResourceIPPools,

148			v4PoolSpec, v6PoolSpec, err := multipool.ParsePoolSpec(poolSpecStr)
149			if err != nil {
150				logger.ErrorContext(ctx,
151					fmt.Sprintf("Failed to parse IP pool spec in %q flag", AutoCreateCiliumResourceIPPools),
152					logfields.PoolName, poolName,
153					logfields.PoolSpec, poolSpecStr,
154					logfields.Error, err)
155				return err
156			}
157	
158			pool := &cilium_v2alpha1_api.CiliumResourceIPPool{
159				ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
160					Name: poolName,
161				},
162				Spec: cilium_v2alpha1_api.ResourceIPPoolSpec{
163					IPv4: v4PoolSpec,
164					IPv6: v6PoolSpec,
165				},
166			}
167	
168			_, err = client.Create(ctx, pool, metav1.CreateOptions{})
169			if err != nil {
170				if k8sErrors.IsAlreadyExists(err) {
171					// Nothing to do, we will not try to update an existing resource
172					logger.InfoContext(ctx,
173						"Found existing CiliumResourceIPPool resource. Skipping creation",
174						logfields.PoolName, poolName)
175				} else {

178						logfields.PoolName, poolName,

181				}

183			}

## The bug

`autoCreatePools` in `operator/pkg/networkdriver/ipam/ipam.go` validated **and** created pools in a single loop. That meant if a later pool spec failed to parse, the earlier pools in the map had *already* been created via the Kubernetes API — a partial, inconsistent result on a startup error.

## The fix

Refactored `autoCreatePools` into a proper **two-pass** approach matching the contract:

1. **Pass 1 — validate everything first:** iterate the entire `poolMap`, parse every spec with `multipool.ParsePoolSpec`, and collect the resulting pool objects. If *any* spec fails to parse, log and return the error immediately — before a single pool is created.
2. **Pass 2 — create all validated pools:** only after all specs pass, `Create` each pool. `AlreadyExists` and any other create errors are logged and skipped (`continue`), never returned — so one existing/failing pool doesn't abort the rest.

Behavior on error is now all-or-nothing for the create phase, which is the point of the requirement.
